about: Hand-written answer key for the REAL evidence of case 009 (Evidence Generation/Cases/Case_009): one CCTV clip, five audio recordings, five text documents. HELD OUT: written before any pipeline run on this evidence was looked at. Events and people keep the generator's ids (cases/CASE_ATM_009.json); each evidence item lists everyone in it, the part they play, and the event they show. The FIR (Evidence Generation 2/Cases/Case_009/Text/FIR_CASE_ATM_009.txt) is an evidence item like any other: every statement in it is mapped from the FIR's own sentences - to an event other evidence also shows, to an event only the FIR states (marked single source), or to context / procedure (the bank's later notice, the officer registering the case, the request for action), which is neither a true event nor an error.

built_from.audio: transcripts from the audio agent's run (Whisper base) and the manifests (start time, source, location). Clip 5 is the re-recorded version (2026-11-22, a different voice from the suspect's).
built_from.video: the video agent's own log (agents/field_agents/video_agent/runs/CASE_ATM_009/CASE_ATM_009_video_log.json) - NOT checked against the clip by a person. Scoring the video agent against this part cannot catch the video agent's own mistakes.
built_from.voices: voice prints computed directly on each speaker's speech (pyannote wespeaker-resnet34): clips 1-4 score 0.70-0.81 against each other, the re-recorded clip 5 scores 0.03-0.12 against all of them - a different speaker. Clips 1-4 have only 1.5-3.2 s of speech each, so their mutual match is weak evidence; it is consistent with one speaker, not proof.

suspect_1.description: the narrator: author of every text (report_20) and the low male-range voice of audio clips 1-4; in the footage, presumably one of the two people leaving
suspect_1.match_appearance: black cap, black hoodie, dark trousers, black shoes
suspect_1.identity_note: Text author <-> voice: linked only by the content continuing one story (on my way / I can see the ATM / in the enclosure / inside), not by identity evidence. Voice clips 1-4: same voice (rough check). Voice/text <-> either person on camera: no evidence. Which of the two people leaving is suspect_1 cannot be told from the evidence; this key assigns the one in the black cap by convention.

findings_an_investigator_should_get.detail: audio4 (10:02:25) says they left 'long before the time mentioned', in the same voice as clips 1-3, while that narrator's own messages put them at the ATM until 10:02:20 ('Done here. Moving.') and the footage shows two people leaving at 10:02:41.

The footage shows two people leaving together; all the narration comes from one person. The second person (grey shirt, backpack) appears only on camera - consistent with the FIR's two suspects, but nothing says who they are or what they did.

'Card working. Cash out now.' (10:01:29) and then 'I've got eyes on the ATM entrance' (10:01:52) and 'Nothing suspicious. Continue.' (10:02:02) read as a lookout's words; whether the narrator or the second person kept watch is not established.
A different voice (audio5, 10:02:49) describes them leaving in a hurry, matching the bystander filmed watching at 10:02:41-50.
The only clip has a low quality score (0.43); appearance details from it are less reliable.

The FIR says two persons went into the booth together; the narrator's own messages from inside say 'Booth is empty' and only one voice narrates - the two are seen together only when leaving (10:02:41).
The FIR names two other onlookers; the evidence shows one bystander on camera and one caller (who may be the same person).
The FIR says one of the two attacked the complainant (Anitha Rao); only the FIR states it.
